36.00878,-79.52075: Battle Of Alamance. The militia under royal Governor Tryon defeated the Regulators at this point, May 16, 1771.
36.07002,-79.78711: Piedmont Railroad. Railroad line between Greensboro and Danville. Constructed, 1862-1864, for the Confederacy. Its terminus was nearby.
36.07021,-79.79057: Lunsford Richardson 1854 1919. A pharmacist and entrepreneur, he created Vicks VapoRub in 1894 while operating a drugstore 150 yards north.
36.07595,-79.78686: Lindsay Street School. The first permanent public graded school in N.C. opened in 1875 in a building which stood on this site.
36.12977,-79.85376: Guilford Courthouse. Armies of Greene and Cornwallis engaged in pivotal battle here on March 15, 1781. Site now U.S. military park.
36.13003,-79.85411: Joseph G. Cannon. Member of Congress for 46 years from Illinois, Speaker of the House, 1903-11. His birthplace stood 1 1/2 miles southwest.
36.49197,-79.76251: 'Land Of Eden'. Near here ran southern line of estate of Wm. Byrd, Virginia planter, author, and surveyor of Va.-N.C. boundary line, 1728.
36.49799,-79.7606: Luther H. Hodges 1898 1974. Governor, 1954-1961; U.S. Secretary of Commerce, 1961-1965. A founder of Research Triangle Park. Home is 100 yards east.
